messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body:
**Blocking: while a section is held, a displaced sibling at the head of its level starves the other processes at that level.**

Take holder H at level 1, its sibling S at level 5, and R, another process's thread, at level 5 behind S.
- **The pick pops S:** §6.3 rule 3's second arm puts S back at the head of level 5 and runs H in its place.
- **At every tick after that:** the first arm finds the outgoing H `Running`, P's section held, and `ready_peek` = S (P's). So H keeps the processor.
- **The result:** nothing ever moves S to the tail, so R never runs while the section is held.

That contradicts rule 4 ("never changes which other process's thread the pick chooses") and §6.4's tick bullet ("round-robin goes on"). It also removes the ground for this sentence: a process that never clears its word holds R off indefinitely. A plain thread of P at level 5 would have given way to R at the end of its slice. `section_confined` has no ready sibling, so it cannot show this.

The held-back sibling has to lose its place as the holder would have: to the tail at a slice end, or the first arm has to compare against the highest ready thread of another process.

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body: **Still open in r2.** §6.3 rule 3's first arm ("if the highest ready thread (`ready_peek`) is P's, the holder stays on the processor") and §6.6's "Other processes keep their round-robin at that level" are r1's text unchanged. So a held section still keeps another process's thread at the holder's level off the processor as long as a displaced sibling heads the level. Full access makes several processes share a level, so this is now the ordinary case, not a corner.

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body:
**A process's own exit or fault leaves `NEED_RESCHED` set across the switch.** This is a wake the sentence above does not cover.

In `teardown_process` (kernel/core/sched.saw at 6ca48b20), `notify_ready(WaitableKind.Process, p)` runs before the caller's thread is invalidated and before `CURRENT_THREAD = NO_THREAD`. When the caller's own process is ending (`ProcessOp.Exit`, or a fault), the caller is still `Running` there. `a_thread_is_running` (irq.saw) is true, so the new compare in `ready_push` sets the flag when it wakes a supervisor at a higher level.

Only `pick_next` clears `NEED_RESCHED`. `resume_after_death` never does. The next thread therefore starts with the flag set, and `stays_running` (`case Running -> not NEED_RESCHED`) gives it a round-robin turn at its first trap that nothing asked for.

Either `resume_after_death` clears the flag, or the compare skips a running thread whose process is tearing down. The case: a supervisor at a higher level parked on a child's Process handle, the child exiting itself, and the supervisor's first trap not requeued.

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body: **Still open in r2.** §5.1 keeps "Joiners woken by `exit_thread` meet an exiting thread, likewise not running" unchanged. Nothing in r2 clears `NEED_RESCHED` for a caller that ends its own process (`ProcessOp.Exit`, or a fault), nor skips the compare while that caller is still `Running`.

messages.body: **This is not what spec says: spec says "The map is immutable after creation."** (spec.md §7, "Per-process map"). `BandMap` sets the map after the create and before the start, so the design changes the rule. §12.1 should rewrite that bullet: immutable from the start, with no remap after. messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer

**Still open in r2, and now in the proposed spec text.**
- **§3.3** still says "The map is immutable from the start on, as spec says".
- **§12.1** keeps the spec's "**The map is immutable after creation.**" bullet as it is, beside a new one saying the launcher sets the map "between the create and the start … The map is immutable from the start."

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body:
**The builder's check is weaker than the convention it stands in for.**
- **Spec §7's mitigation (a):** "servers run at ≥ the max priority of their clients".
- **This check:** it compares only the client's `Normal` level against the server's.
- **Why it matters:** with eight bands a client can map `High` or `Band4` to `Band7` above the server's levels while its `Normal` sits below. §7 relies on this check to keep inversion out.

To match the convention, compare the client's highest mapped level against the server's lowest, or say which of the server's levels the check means. A builder test then needs a client whose `High` alone is above the server.

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body: **Still open in r2, and wider.** §10.2's check still compares `Normal` only. Under full access it can't express the convention, while r2's spec text now claims the builder enforces it. Details are in the new thread on §10.2.

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body:
**`rt_arena_two_levels` is red only if the Timer fires while the Low thread is inside the arena window.**

That is a matter of timing, which §14's opening rules out ("made true by construction ... no wait on the clock"). `rt_alloc` takes the arena only when `heap_alloc(DEFAULT_HEAP, …)` answers 0 (rt/common/src/lib.saw). If the fire lands outside the window, the High thread allocates without contention, and the case passes with the window left outside the section.

The case needs a construction that puts the High thread's wake inside the window, for example the Low thread signalling from inside it through a test-only hook, or the case should say why the window is always open when the fire lands.

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body: **Still open in r2.** §14.5's `rt_arena_two_levels` row is unchanged. Nothing puts the High thread's wake inside the Low thread's arena window, and r2 doesn't say why it would always land there. As written, the case's red still depends on timing.

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body:
**The output lock's own `SpinLock` window is still a spin at two levels.**

`OUTPUT` is a std `SpinLock<OutputState>` (rt/common/src/lib.saw). This design parks the logical lock's waiters, but a waiter counts itself in the state by taking that `SpinLock` first. Today the comment says a thread "loses the processor inside it only to a tick". With preemption on wake it can also lose the processor to a wake.

A Low thread preempted inside that short window leaves a High sibling spinning on the `SpinLock` with the Low thread never run. That is the same livelock this section fixes for the arena.

The state window makes no call that parks, so it can run inside the section as the arena's and heaps' do. Alternatively, say why it cannot be preempted.

The parked lock also has no inheritance. A High waiter behind a Low holder of the output lock waits on every level between them. §7's "no inheritance" argument should say that this case is accepted.

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body:
**Half answered.** §7's inheritance lock removes the `SpinLock` window for a waiter and a holder that both have a block. I walked a Low holder preempted at each point of §7.2's take and give with a High sibling arriving, and none of them spins.

The same spin survives where §8.3 keeps today's behavior: "one that meets an anonymous holder, or has no block itself, yields as today". That case is in the new thread on §8.3.

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body:
**The record starts at the claim, so time with the line asserted and unclaimed is not measured.**
- **Where a line is claimed:** only through `service_irq` (`deliver_line(hal.irq_claim(cause), …)`, irq.saw) on a trap, at the idle poll, or at a preemption point.
- **What goes uncounted:** while the kernel runs with interrupts masked through an operation with no preemption point, the asserted line waits unclaimed. Spec §9's "What takes no point" lists teardown, console writes and the UART spin. The trap's own entry also comes before the stamp.
- **Why it matters:** "That is trap, funnel, …" overstates what is measured, and §5.3 says this delay is what SO-103 underestimates.

Either §11 states the record's lower edge, or the stamp comes from something that sees the assertion: a hardware timestamp, or the time the line was last seen idle.

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body: **Still open in r2.** §11 still says the record runs "from the kernel's claim of a fire", and §12.4 that "The kernel stamps each fire's claim". The time a line spends asserted before the kernel claims it is still outside the record, and "That is trap, funnel, …" still reads as if it were the whole latency. Saying where the record starts would settle it.

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body:
**Several checks the design adds have no case in §14.** By the owner's standard, each needs a case that goes red when the check is removed, or a named equivalent with a reason:
- **The pair placement (§6.2):** a pair in an image row without write, and a pair straddling two rows. Only `section_map_row` covers this answer.
- **`section_at` cleared when the body is freed:** a later process in the same record must not inherit the word.
- **The `Latency` record:** its copy door's fault (§11).
- **The builder:** the `SOS_IMAGE_BUILDER=python` refusal, and the stock root's `root: bands NAME: STATUS` stop (§10.4).
- **`BandMap`'s `level_cap` update:** `band_map_above_cap`'s launcher map tops at 1, and a skipped update is red there only if an unmapped child's default `level_cap` is not also 1. The design does not say what that default is. Say it, and pick a launcher map whose top differs from the default.

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body:
**Still open in r2.** None of the five checks gets a case.
- **§14.3's section refusals** are still `section_map_row`, `section_unaligned`, `section_twice`, `section_not_self`, `section_denied` and `section_unregistered`.
- **§14.7** is still `latency_counts`, `latency_pending` and `latency_denied`.

**`band_map_above_cap` may be blind.** It maps a child at 2 under a launcher given the simple map. r2 never states an unmapped child's `level_cap` as a number. §3.2 ("A process no launcher maps has it") and §3.3 ("A child given the simple map holds level 1") together suggest 1. Then the launcher's own map tops out at the default, and a skipped cap update leaves the case green. Stating the default, and giving the launcher a map whose top differs from it, would settle it.

**r2's new ops have checks without cases too:**
- `LockWait` step 2's copy-door refusal (`lock_unaligned` is `BadAlign` only);
- step 6's "anything but a Thread" arm (`lock_foreign_owner` is a Thread of another process);
- `LockWake`'s own answers, none of which has a case.

messages.body: **This contradicts §6.7**, which says "`enter()` on an unregistered word panics". §8.3 puts the arena and heap windows inside the section, and a single-threaded program never registers (it makes no thread through `thread_create(run:)`). anchor.exact: a client whose `Normal` level is above its server's

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body:
**This check can't enforce the convention under full access, and r2's spec text now says it does.**

§12.1 rewrites mitigation (a) as "the convention that servers run at ≥ the max priority of their clients (… the image builder refuses a stock-root image that breaks it)". This rule compares `Normal` only. The builder knows two maps (simple, top 1; full, top 7), so it can't see the band a client calls from or the band a server serves at.
- **Full client, full server:** C's `Normal` 2 against S's 2 is accepted. But C's `Rt3` thread at 7 can call S while S serves at `Normal`, which §3.5 has every service do ("take full access and serve at `Normal`, level 2"). Any thread between them, such as the radio's Wi-Fi task at 3, then preempts S while C's level-7 thread waits.
- **Comparing the client's highest level instead** would refuse §3.5's own layout, where full-access services are clients of the radio's serve thread at 2.

So either the declaration states the band each client calls from and the band each server serves at, and the builder compares those, or §12.1 and this rule say the check covers `Normal` only and the rest is the image author's.

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body:
**"Yields as today" keeps r1's spin for these two paths, at any level gap.**
- **No block:** today's yield does nothing for a thread with no block. `rt.saw`'s `sos_rt_yield` says its wait "spins until a tick moves it".
- **With a block:** the yield returns the thread to its own level. The output lock's comment in `rt/common` says that scheme "relies on the scheduler's one ready list: a waiter in a higher priority band than the holder would never let it run".

**Who has no block:** only sosmain's main thread and `thread_create(run:)` threads get one. A thread made through the C floor's `sos_process_thread_create` has none.

**It takes only the simple map:**
1. A `_start` or C program starts a floor-made worker at `Background` (0).
2. The worker takes the output lock anonymously.
3. The main thread at 1 wakes from a Timer, preempts it, and prints.
4. The main thread's wait yields, or does nothing, and the tick re-picks it (§9: "Lower levels wait for higher ones to block"). The worker never runs again.

Either these paths are confined to one level (refused, or the lock held anonymously only by a process that has one level), or the design says how a thread with no block parks.

anchor.prefix: int inside a section is legal

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body:
**Not every wait for the output lock parks, so this rule misses two cases.**
- **A hang with no diagnostic:** a thread with no block, or one that meets an anonymous holder, waits by yielding (§8.3), not by parking. Inside its section, printing while a sibling holds the output lock, rule 7 never fires. Rule 3 then keeps it on the processor ahead of the sibling that holds the lock, so it hangs, even at one level.
- **A panic loses its text:** the panic sink takes the output lock before it writes anything (`rt/common`'s `rt_panic`). A thread with a block that panics inside a user section while a sibling holds the output lock parks in the sink. Per the owner's ruling it's then faulted `SectionHeld`, and the panic's text is never printed.

The second one wants the sink exempt, or the fault record carrying the panic. The first wants the yield paths named here.

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body:
**A raise can outlive its waiter.** `LockWake` lowers its caller, and §7.3 lowers only "the holder's" level at the give. That misses one interleaving.

Take one full-access process with L (`Low`, 1), M (`High`, 3, compute-bound), W (`Rt0`, 4) and X (`Rt1`, 5):
1. L takes the lock. W waits, so L is raised to 4.
2. L's give swaps `owner` to 0. Before L loads `waiters`, an interrupt wakes X, which preempts L.
3. X takes the lock and gives it back. It finds `waiters` nonzero and calls `LockWake`, which wakes W and writes `waiters` to 0. X, the caller, is "lowered", and nothing changes.
4. L resumes, loads `waiters` = 0, and doesn't trap.

L is still at 4, above M, with no waiter naming it. That breaks §7.3's own definition of a level, and the promise that a holder is raised "until it gives the lock back". If `LockWake` recomputed the level of each woken waiter's `lock_holder`, not only its caller's, this would close.

anchor.suffix: for a thread with no block),

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body:
**"The anonymous word" needs defining.**
- **If it's one word shared by every thread with no block,** the runtime's recursion test (`state.owner == me` today) lets two such threads both "hold" the lock, and their lines interleave. `tests/lock-wait`, two `_start` threads, would show it.
- **If it's one per thread,** the design has to say how it's made. Today's identity, `(n << 1) | 1` in `rt.saw`, has a nonzero low byte, so §7.2's kernel would read it as a handle word. The first such number, 3, is §12's boot Thread handle word.

anchor.exact: handle from its block. The runtime's output lock is one

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body:
**A task made through the C floor has no block**, and the floor exports no way to make one: blocks come only from sosmain's start-up and the `thread_create(run:)` trampoline. So when the radio's adapter builds FreeRTOS mutexes on `sos_lock_take`, a task made through `sos_process_thread_create` gets no inheritance and waits as in the thread on §8.3.

Under full access, a BT controller task at `Rt1` (5) waiting on a mutex the Wi-Fi task at `High` (3) holds would spin for good. Either the floor gains a way to give a thread its block, or the adapter makes its tasks through a path that does; SO-103's adapter design would settle which.

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body:
**With no image veto, a full-access process can starve the stock root.**
- **The starvation:** root runs at level 1 in every image. The scheduler has strict priority and no aging (§9). So any package declaring `bands = "full"` that spins at `Normal` (2) or above keeps root off the processor for good.
- **What it breaks:** §6.6's "A supervisor that wants a wedged process gone kills it" then doesn't hold for a full-access process under the stock root.

The ruling granted full access as asked, so this is a consequence to state, not a refusal to add. Placing the stock root above what it grants would avoid it, if that's wanted.
